headline: Growth accelerates and backlog swells, but losses widen
summary_short: Revenue jumped 112% y/y to $2,575M and revenue backlog reached roughly $104B, but net loss widened to $626M on sharply higher interest expense following this quarter's debt raises.
summary_long: Revenue rose 112% y/y and 24% q/q to $2,575M as AI infrastructure demand accelerated; backlog reached ~$104B, plus $25B of new Q3 commitments. GAAP operating income swung to a $49M loss (from +$19M) as infrastructure costs more than doubled, though adjusted EBITDA still grew 100% y/y to $1,510M — the gap is mostly D&A and stock comp, not core opex bloat. Net loss widened to $626M (from $290M), almost entirely on interest expense, which jumped to $640M after a $3.1B term loan, a $1B Jane Street investment, and over $10B of new debt/convertibles this quarter. Cash rose to $5,524M. On the call, management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $12.4-13.2B and guided Q3 revenue to $3.45-3.6B.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes growth to accelerating customer demand and broadening enterprise adoption, citing new or expanded relationships with Bentley Systems, Caterpillar, Grammarly, Databricks and others, plus active power capacity growing nearly 500 MW.
Swing to a GAAP operating loss is explained by technology-and-infrastructure expense growing to $1,507M (+125% y/y), outpacing 112% revenue growth, while sales/marketing and G&A grew more slowly.

Widening is driven almost entirely by interest expense (-$640M vs -$267M y/y), consistent with this quarter's $3.1B term loan and over $10B of new unsecured debt/convertible issuance funding infrastructure buildout.

Non-GAAP EBITDA still grew 100% y/y despite the GAAP operating loss because D&A ($1,393M) and stock-based comp ($165M) are added back before interest and taxes, isolating the loss to financing and non-cash items.

CEO cited an "inflection point" where scale is beginning to convert into operating leverage; the release highlights Nasdaq-100 inclusion and a $104B backlog (plus $25B of new Q3 commitments) as demand evidence ahead of the raised FY2026 guidance.
